text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- A New York state assembly hearing on the World War Two role of Swiss banks trook place in a more objective and relaxed atmosphere than a similar New York city heairng this week. Politicians and Jewish leaders voiced approval for Swiss efforts to uncover the past. Swiss Foreign Minster Flavio Cotti invited World Jewish Congress general secretary Israel Singer to Switzerland.
- Berne-based department store Loeb posted sales of 244.9 million Swiss francs in fiscal 1996/97, up 4.1 percent. Net profit stagnated at 9.1 million Swiss francs.

- Federal prosecutor Carla Del Ponte, taking unusual steps to find whoever leaked a secret diplomatic report to media, called on anonymous tipsters to get in touch with her office. She is investigating how Swiss media got ahold of a report by the Swiss ambassador to the U.S., who resigned when his comments on "waging a war" against Jewish critics were published.
- Swiss consumer confidence index climbed by 3 points to minus 35 between October and January.
- The number of people who received Swiss citizenship in 1996 rose by 15 percent to 20,077 persons compared to the previous year.

- Typical Swiss family structures have changed significantly in the last ten years, accoridng to a major survey. The Swiss get married later, have fewer childern, and more families have both parents working, the Federal Office for Statistics wrote.

- Switzerland should ban private traffic on all roads on four Sundays a year and open the streets for pedestrians, bicyclists and roller skaters, according to a group organising a drive for a national referendum on its proposal.
